messages:
anna: Heads-up — did a quick microbudget pass on the new 9B-int6 candidate. Want to share a tiny handoff before GTN sync.

sam: nice. short summary?

anna: TL;DR: quality delta vs our 13B baseline is small on multi-turn QA (+1.7% exact match on our slices) but inference cost per request is ~38% lower when using int6 + lru-prefix cache. p95 latency slightly higher (~50ms) on cold KV.

priya: can you paste the numbers? product needs a clear budget threshold for rollout.

anna: sure — sample from synthetic slice (avg length 3 turns):
```
baseline-13b-fp16: cost/request $0.0124, p50 78ms, p95 310ms, EM 71.2%
candidate-9b-int6: cost/request $0.0077, p50 82ms, p95 360ms, EM 69.5%
```
Note: cost computed including KV cache hit-rate at ~22% in this slice.

luis: that cost delta is attractive. Product wants a hard per-request ceiling for GTN pilot. What's reasonable?

sam: propose microbudget ceiling = $0.009 per request for interactive feature (3-turn avg). If candidate stays under that, we can route 30% traffic.

priya: product note: GTN agreed to 15% quality slack vs baseline for a cost-driven pilot, but they'd prefer latency not exceed p95 400ms.

anna: candidate fits those constraints in our sims (p95 360ms). Two caveats: 1) some long-context queries (20+ tokens) push p95 to ~460ms when cold; 2) certain safety prompts showed regressed calibration on one language slice.

luis: safety regressions — can you point to repro?

anna: uploaded mini-slice to S3 (link: https://s3.redwood/slices/1738-microbudget-safety). Example failing prompt: `system: avoid toxic content` + user asking for rephrasing of violent text. Model sometimes paraphrases too literally.

priya: that's a blocker for GTN unless we mitigate at serving layer. Any quick mitigations?

anna: options: 
- soft-routing: send safety-sensitive prompts to 13B baseline via classifier (~1.2% of traffic). Cheap but adds routing complexity.
- response-level filter + post-processing heuristics (run safety-checker extra token cost ~$0.0008 per checked request).
- apply small preference/bias in prompt template (low lift) — needs eval.

sam: vote for classifier routing for pilot. Keeps quality deterministic and avoids per-response extra checks.

luis: agree. classifier thresh should aim to capture 95% of safety risks, keep routing cost blowup < 8% of overall spend.

anna: implemented quick classifier: `safety_score = model.embed(prompt) -> logistic`. On a 10k eval slice classifier recall ~94% at 0.3 threshold (false positive 0.9%). With routing, blended cost/request becomes:
```
blended-cost = 0.99 * 0.0077 + 0.01 * 0.0124 = $0.00787
```
so still below microbudget $0.009.

priya: great. For GTN handoff, please include rollout plan and rollback triggers.

anna: draft plan: 
- Phase A (canary 2%): route vanilla traffic, monitor p95, EM on production slices, and safety classifier false negatives.
- Phase B (ramp 2->30% over 5 days): step ramp, keep canary baseline fallback 100% for flagged requests.
- Rollback triggers: >5% drop in EM vs baseline on production slice OR p95 > 420ms for >30m OR safety FN incidents > 2 in 24h.

sam: add cost guardrail: if spend per-unique-user increases >12% for the pilot cohort, pause ramp.

luis: ops question: memory/instance footprint for 9B-int6 on dedicated — any special infra needs?

anna: uses 80% of a standard gpool slot (we measured). No extra infra changes for dedicated; for private customers need to check HSM constraints but irrelevant for GTN hosted.

deploybot: deploy check: canary bundle built (img: infer-9b-int6:2026-11-09-rc1). Canary config saved at /deploy/canary/1738001234.json

priya: handoff checklist for GTN: 
- Confirm classifier routing config saved and tested (anna)
- Add rollback rules to console (sam)
- Product-facing note summarizing quality tradeoffs and microbudget target (priya)
- Post-mortem/notes link for early regressions (if any)

anna: I'll put a short README in the S3 slice dir with these numbers and links. Also adding two microtests to the CI that check EM delta < 7% and p95 < 420ms over last 24h sample.

sam: perfect. thanks anna — feel free to start canary when you have monitoring dashboards wired.

anna: starting canary tomorrow 10:30 PT unless objections. :rocket:

priya: no objections from product. Good luck. :crossed_fingers:

luis: ping me if the classifier numbers change.

anna: will do.
